stock: P265/70R17 on 17-inch steel or alloy wheels (standard, per Toyota's 2014 specs)
265/75R16 / LT265/75R16 BFGoodrich on 16-inch TRD wheels (TRD and Trail Teams trucks)

max_tire.note: One owner's only rubbed the driver's-side mud flap under compression, cured by heating and flattening it. A stricter IH8MUD view: only 31–32 in clears in every situation without a body mount chop.
Slee told one owner this is the limit without body trimming; owners run it on factory wheels with no rub. ARB told another owner 285/75R17.

Owners run 305/70R17s and 34s with chopped mounts and plastic trim removed; one still rubs at full compression. A club pair on 35s touches only at extreme flex and full lock. Watch wheel backspacing: wide tires on factory wheels hit the upper control arm.

items.title: Rear access-door panels can crack at the seat-belt retractor
items.summary: The front seat-belt retractors mount in the rear-hinged access doors; repeated hard slamming can crack the door panel.

items.title: Intermediate steering shaft weld
items.summary: The shaft linking the steering wheel to the steering gear may have an inadequate weld; dealers replace it.

items.title: Trail Teams Ultimate Edition front suspension bolts
items.summary: Lower ball-joint and lower-arm bolts may have been under-torqued when the TRD shocks and springs were fitted; dealers check and retighten them.

items.title: TRD brake kit outer brake tube
items.summary: On trucks with dealer-fitted TRD front brake kits, a balance weight can damage the outer brake tube and leak fluid; the tube is replaced.

items.title: Toyota auxiliary driving lamps too bright
items.summary: Bumper-mounted accessory lamps with 55 W bulbs exceed high-beam limits; dealers fit 35 W bulbs.

items.title: TPMS not recalibrated after accessory wheels
items.summary: Trucks given accessory wheels and LT tires before sale may not warn at the required pressure; FJs can't be recalibrated, so dealers replace the TPMS control unit.

items.title: Denso low-pressure fuel pump
items.summary: Added to Toyota's fuel-pump recall in March 2020; the pump can fail and stall the engine. Dealers replace it.

tsbs.title: 6-speed manual clutch release bearing squeak or rattle
tsbs.summary: 2007–2011 FJ Cruiser 6MT: replace the release bearing, fork support and release cylinder with updated parts.

tsbs.title: Harsh downshift into first after sitting in Drive
tsbs.summary: 2007–2013 FJ Cruiser and Tacoma 4x4s: replacement rear driveshaft once the shaft is confirmed as the cause; greasing a dry slip yoke often cures it.

timeline.change: FJ Cruiser concept shown in Voodoo Blue at the Detroit auto show
Production version shown at the Chicago auto show in February; Hino starts building it at Hamura in January 2006
Launch: 239-hp 1GR-FE on premium, six-speed manual (full-time 4WD) or five-speed automatic; 3,200 TRD Special Editions. Inner fender aprons on 2007 and some early 2008 trucks can bulge and crack
Side curtain and torso airbags standard; first Trail Teams Special Edition (Iceberg, 3,200 built)
Optional backup camera; no Trail Teams edition, a TRD package instead. US sales fall to 11,941
Dual VVT-i 1GR-FE: 259 hp on regular fuel, slightly better economy
260 hp; new front-seat hinges for easier rear-seat access; RHD sales begin in Australia and New Zealand
CRAWL control on Trail Teams automatics; access-door panel recall covers 2007–2013 trucks
Final US model year; 2,500 Trail Teams Ultimate Editions in Heritage Blue
Australian exports end in August 2016; Japan Final Edition in September 2017, Japanese sales end January 2018
Middle East Final Edition (1,000 units); production ends in December

identify.intro: There was essentially one US trim, so what you're checking is the drivetrain, the engine generation and whether a claimed special edition is real.

items.head: VIN and plant
items.body: US FJs start with JT and were built by Hino at Hamura, Japan. The 10th character is the model year (7 = 2007, A = 2010, E = 2014). 4x4s are GSJ15 and 4x2s GSJ10. On Bring a Trailer, 2007 VINs begin JTEBU11F and 2010–2014 VINs begin JTEBU4BF.

items.head: Manual or automatic 4WD
items.body: Manual trucks have full-time 4WD with a center-differential lock and no 2WD position. Automatic 4x4s have a part-time transfer case with 2H, and automatics were also sold as 4x2s with no transfer-case lever.

items.head: Locker and A-TRAC
items.body: Look for the rear-locker and A-TRAC switches on the dash. The locker was standard with the manual and optional with the automatic (2014 spec), so don't assume every automatic has one.

items.head: Trail Teams editions
items.body: Trail Teams trucks are monotone in that year's color, with blacked-out mirrors, handles and bumper caps, Trail Teams badges and TRD wheels. The 2014 Ultimate Edition is Heritage Blue with a white grille surround and a 'One of 2500' dash plaque. Badges are easy to copy, so ask for the window sticker.

items.head: TRD Special Edition
items.body: The 2007 TRD Special Edition is Black Diamond with a black roof (other FJs have a white roof), with TRD Bilsteins, rock rails, a cat-back exhaust and gunmetal TRD wheels; 3,200 were built.

items.head: Engine generation
items.body: 2007–2009 trucks have the single VVT-i engine (239 hp, premium fuel); 2010–2014 trucks have dual VVT-i (259–260 hp, regular).

values.intro: Jalopnik found sub-100,000-mile FJs listed at or above their last new price. Mileage, rust history and the 2010+ engine drive the spread, and special editions earn a premium only when they're clean.
values.note: Based on 20 Bring a Trailer sales, August–October 2026: $12,500 for a 2007 up to $56,250 for a 7,000-mile 2014. A 27,000-mile 2014 Ultimate Edition sold for $42,000, and a 6,000-mile 2008 for $43,900.

paragraphs: Every US-market FJ Cruiser (2007–2014) is federally legal. The right-hand-drive Japanese and Australian trucks (sold from late 2010 and 2011) and the FJs built for the Middle East and other markets until 2022 were never certified for the US, so under NHTSA's 25-year rule they can't be imported until each is 25 years old, which for the earliest RHD trucks means about 2035. Canada sold 4x4 FJs alongside the US,.
